Commentary.Commentary: Chris Morris was the other bowler to rake in 3 wickets, including the scalp of the top-scoring Bravo. Imran Tahir did well to restrict the batsmen but was unable to pick up any wickets despite several close calls. We expect West Indies will feel the pressure to hold the South African batsmen back and keep the run-rate down to gain a bonus point and advance into the finals of the tri-series. Stay tuned for the run chase.

South Africa's bowling was a good mix of pace and spin despite the large amounts of wides given. The fielders also impressed with their timely stops and catches. Kagiso Rabada got the Proteas' bowling attack off to a lightning quick start, delivering some fantastic pace that the batsmen had difficulty facing. He turned in his 10 overs with a miserly economy rate of 3.1 and took 3 wickets.

A 156-run partnership lasting 150 balls ensued that took the home side from the verge of collapse to a position of great stability. Pollard was finally removed on 62 but Bravo went on to score his century before getting dismissed by another fantastic catch by du Plessis. Holder got off to a slow start, facing 16 balls without scoring but once he got off the mark, he batted powerfully to put up a 54-run stand with Brathwaite. But with his dismissal, the lower-middle order was not able to accompany Brathwaite successfully and the Windies lost the plot as they managed only 25/4 in the last 6 overs.

Thus ends a competitive innings by the West Indies. The hosts were off to a rocky start, losing wickets at a prodigious rate and unable to pull in the runs. Five overs in and the score was 21/4. However, Darren Bravo stood his ground and with the arrival of Kieron Pollard, the fortunes of the Windies took an upward turn.

It is referred upstairs and replays show that while completing the run, Gabriel collided with Amla as he came forward from short mid-wicket to collect the throw. That collision made Gabriel fall an inch short. Brathwaite tried to protest with de Villiers but the appeal was made. WEST INDIES HAVE BEEN BOWLED OUT FOR 285!

OUT! That is another stunner from Faf du Plessis! Ends a terrific knock from Darren Bravo. Just when West Indies were looking to step the ante, the Proteas get a wicket. A slower ball around off, 119 kph, shorter in length, Bravo looks to go over mid on, seeing the field up. However, he is early into the stroke and gets a top edge. The ball seems to have enough on it to clear mid on but Faf du Plessis runs back and dives full length to take a blinder. He then lies spread-eagled on the field as AB de Villiers comes across from long off to hug him. The crowd stands in unison to applaud Bravo off the field. What a knock. And what a catch. Good cricket.

Full on off, defended off the front foot to the covers.
Length ball on middle and off, tucked to square leg for a single.
Bravo plays a forward defence to cover.
Full and just outside off, 147.8 kph, Pollard defends it watchfully.
Bouncer! The batsman does well to evade it.
This is on the stumps, watchfully defended.
FOUR LEG BYES! Down the leg side, 145.8 kph, Pollard gets across to tuck and the ball goes off his pads to fine leg.
TOP EDGE! SAFE! Short on off, Bravo looks to defend it but gets a top edge and the ball is lobbed over backward point. The batsmen pick up a single.
Full outside off, Bravo looks to defend but is beaten as the ball swings away.
Shorter ball outside off, Bravo guides it to third man for a single.
Fuller on middle and off, well defended.

Length ball on off, blocked with a straight bat to the off side.

Bravo manages only a bottom edge on that one. The batsmen have run through for a single.
KIERON POLLARD walks in at number 6, replacing Ramdin.

OUT! Ramdin is double bluffed and Rabada has bowled an absolute beauty here! After seeing the way Ramdin played the previous ball, AB de Villiers stationed himself at deepish short leg. That planted a seed of a short ball in Ramdin's mind. He was back to this one but then Rabada smartly slipped in a full ball, almost close to a yorker, on middle. Ramdin looked to flick but missed. The ball hit the middle stump. Rabada is on a roll here. 3-0-9-3!

BANG! ON THE HELMET! That was a nasty bouncer. Dug in short outside off, 140.2 kph, Ramdin initially comes forward but then takes his eyes off the ball. It hits him on the left shoulder and then onto the helmet, just beneath the ear. Thankfully, he is okay.
FOUR! A rare loose ball, short and down the leg side, Ramdin works it to the fine leg fence.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Fuller on middle, driven straight to mid on.
Good length ball around middle and off, tapped towards short mid-wicket.
Outside off, left alone.
On middle and leg, worked straight to mid-wicket.
Outside off, another play and a miss.
The batsman was beaten and missed the line of the delivery.
FOUR! Down the leg side, nudged to the fine leg fence.
The batsman chooses to leave the ball outside his off stump.
The batsman was beaten and missed the line of the delivery. Just a run and 2 wickets from the over, Rabada has figures of 2-0-5-2!
WIDE. A nervous hat-trick ball, down the leg side, left alone.
DENESH RAMDIN walks in at number 5, replacing Samuels.

OUT! Lock, stock and barrel! The hero of the previous game, has gone for a zero in this one! Wow, wow, wow, Kagiso, Kagiso, Rabada. A terrific yorker around off, 146.2 kph, Samuels is a bit lazy and as a result, late in getting his bat down. The ball goes beneath the bat and shatters the stumps! Bye, bye, see you later. West Indies' innings is similar to that of the stumps right now - total disarray.
MARLON SAMUELS walks in at number 4, replacing Charles.

OUT! Edged and taken! In next to no time, West Indies have lost both their openers. A length ball wide outside off, 146 kph, Charles pushes at it and gets a thick outside edge. Simple catch for Morris at second slip.
Outside off, a play and a miss.

OUT! Edged and taken! Parnell has struck. A length ball wide outside off, angling away, 141.3 kph, Fletcher throws his bat at it and gets a thick outside edge. Simple catch to de Kock.
The batsman shoulders arms to let that one through.
A swing and a miss this time outside off.
FOUR! Fine shot! Fractionally short in length outside off, Fletcher cuts it behind point and the ball races away. Big Morne Morkel dives to his right but parries the ball across the ropes.
FOUR! A bit ugly but effective. A length ball around off, Fletcher heaves it over mid on for a boundary!
Full and outside off, pushed straight to point.
WAYNE PARNELL will bowl from the other end!
Short ball outisde off, Charles misses his cut and the ball goes to the keeper.
Length ball outside leg, Charles is hit on the pads.

Back of a length ball, steered to point.

The umpires and players have made their way out to the middle. It will be JOHNSON CHARLES and ANDRE FLETCHER who will open the batting for the hosts. KAGISO RABADA will start off with the bowling proceedings. Here we go!!!
TOSS - South Africa win the toss and opt to bowl!

South Africa leads with 12 points to West Indies' 8 but that won't matter as the outcome of the match will decide the second finalist of the series. The Proteas batting attack has been good so far, with the exception of a damp AB de Villiers, and we can expect a strong showing from them. Can the inconsistent Windies pull through or will we expect to see the steady South African side emerge victorious? Stay tuned for the toss.

Hello and a warm welcome to the final league match of the Tri-series between West Indies and South Africa. The winner of this match will go on to face Australia in the finals. Despite a high-scoring performance by Marlon Samuels, West Indies faced disappointment as they lost out to Australia. Another cause for concern is skipper Jason Holder's fitness as he limped off the field with a hamstring injury after bowling a couple overs in the last match.
